practiceQuestions.q: When did the Constituent Assembly of India hold its very first meeting?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly held its first meeting on 9 December 1946 in the Constitution Hall (now the Central Hall of Parliament House).

practiceQuestions.q: Who served as the temporary/provisional President of the Constituent Assembly during its first meeting?
practiceQuestions.sol: Following the French practice, Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member, was elected as the temporary President of the Assembly.

practiceQuestions.q: When was Dr. Rajendra Prasad elected as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December 1946.

practiceQuestions.q: Who presented the historic 'Objectives Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic 'Objectives Resolution' on 13 December 1946, which later formed the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: On which date was the National Flag of India adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Flag of India on 22 July 1947, just prior to India's independence.

practiceQuestions.q: When did the Constituent Assembly finally adopt the Constitution of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constitution of India was adopted, enacted, and given to themselves by the people through the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949.

practiceQuestions.q: How many total sessions did the Constituent Assembly hold for the framing of the Constitution?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to complete its task, holding a total of 11 sessions.

practiceQuestions.q: When did the Constituent Assembly hold its final session?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly held its final session on 24 January 1950, when it unanimously elected Dr. Rajendra Prasad as the first President of India.

practiceQuestions.q: Who served as the Constitutional Advisor (Legal Advisor) to the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sir B.N. Rau was appointed as the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly, preparing the initial draft of the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: On which date did India formally become a member of the Commonwealth of Nations, as ratified by the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: India's membership of the Commonwealth of Nations was ratified by the Constituent Assembly in May 1949, acknowledging its continuation as a member despite becoming a republic.

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the Constituent Assembly forced to function in a dual capacity (as a constituent body and a legislative body)?
opts: The British Parliament abolished the Indian Legislative Assembly prior to transferring power.
Under the Indian Independence Act of 1947, the Assembly became a sovereign legislature tasked with enacting ordinary laws for the transitional period until a new parliament was elected.
The Muslim League members demanded simultaneous law-making powers before participating.
The Supreme Court mandated that constitutional drafting cannot occur without a functional legislative background.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 made the Constituent Assembly a fully sovereign body and declared it as the Dominion legislature. Thus, whenever it met as a constituent body, it was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, and when it met as a legislative body, it was chaired by G.V. Mavalankar.

practiceQuestions.q: Who presided over the Constituent Assembly when it met to perform its legislative functions (as India's first Parliament)?
practiceQuestions.sol: When the Constituent Assembly met as a legislative body, G.V. Mavalankar presided over its meetings, distinguishing its legislative role from its constituent role under Dr. Rajendra Prasad.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best captures the dual role performed by the Constituent Assembly from November 1946 to March 1952?
opts: Drafting the Constitution and acting as a judicial appellate tribunal.
Framing the Constitution and enacting ordinary laws for the country.
Conducting general elections and negotiating foreign treaties with British colonies.
Reorganizing princely states and formulating the Five-Year Plans.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly performed two primary tasks: making the Constitution and enacting ordinary laws for the country, effectively functioning as the Provisional Parliament of India until 1952.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the profound significance of the 'Objectives Resolution' adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
opts: It established Hindi as the sole national language of India.
It laid down the fundamental principles, philosophy, and socio-economic goals that shaped the framing of the Constitution.
It formally dissolved the Princely States and integrated them into British India provinces.
It created the post of the Prime Minister and defined federal division of powers.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Objectives Resolution provided the ideological anchor and foundational values—such as sovereignty, justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity—which were later crystallized in the Preamble.

practiceQuestions.q: In addition to constitution-making and legislation, what crucial nation-building function was performed by the Constituent Assembly in May 1949?
opts: Ratification of India's membership of the Commonwealth.
Adoption of the National Anthem and National Song.
Abolition of the privy purses of princely rulers.
practiceQuestions.sol: India's decision to remain in the Commonwealth of Nations was ratified by the Constituent Assembly in May 1949, reconciling membership with republican status.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best describes the legal nature of the Constituent Assembly prior to the Indian Independence Act of 1947?
opts: A fully sovereign body created by the Indian National Congress.
A limited body whose creation was recommended by the Cabinet Mission Plan and constrained by British proposals.
An executive council appointed directly by the Viceroy of India.
An elected parliament of independent India with unlimited powers from day one.
practiceQuestions.sol: Initially, the Constituent Assembly was a body framed under the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) with restricted authority. It became a fully sovereign body only after the enactment of the Indian Independence Act, 1947.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Constituent Assembly ensure wide public participation and input during the constitution-making process?
opts: By conducting nationwide universal adult suffrage referendums on each constitutional article.
By publishing the draft constitution in public domains, inviting critiques, public feedback, and debates in the press.
By allowing every Indian citizen to cast a vote in the Constituent Assembly elections.
By holding compulsory village-level panchayat hearings supervised by British officials.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Drafting Committee published the draft Constitution in newspapers and public domains, inviting suggestions and criticisms from the public, press, and provincial assemblies, ensuring deep democratic deliberation.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following constitutional milestones was completed by the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950?
opts: Enactment of the Representation of the People Act.
Adoption of the National Anthem and National Song, and election of the first President of India.
Passing of the First Constitutional Amendment Act.
practiceQuestions.sol: On 24 January 1950, during its final session, the Constituent Assembly adopted the National Anthem, the National Song, and unanimously elected Dr. Rajendra Prasad as the first President of India.

practiceQuestions.q: What constitutional mechanism permitted certain provisions of the Indian Constitution to come into force immediately on 26 November 1949?
opts: A special ordinance issued by Lord Mountbatten.
Article 394 of the Constitution itself, which specified provisions that would come into force immediately.
A royal decree signed by King George VI.
A directive issued by the Drafting Committee Chairman B.R. Ambedkar.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 394 stated that provisions relating to citizenship, elections, provisional parliament, temporary and transitional provisions, and short title would come into force on 26 November 1949, while the rest came into force on 26 January 1950.

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the date 26 January specifically chosen for the full commencement of the Indian Constitution, despite its adoption on 26 November 1949?
opts: It marked the anniversary of the Cabinet Mission Plan arrival.
It commemorated the Purna Swaraj day declared in 1930 under the Congress Lahore session.
It coincided with the retirement date of the last British Governor-General.
It was astrologically deemed the most auspicious day by traditional scholars.
practiceQuestions.sol: 26 January was chosen because it was on this day in 1930 that the 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) resolution was promulgated by the Indian National Congress following the Lahore session of December 1929.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the functions of the Constituent Assembly:
1. It functioned exclusively as a constitution-drafting body until January 1950 and undertook no other governance tasks.
2. When the Constituent Assembly met as a legislative body, it was chaired by G.V. Mavalankar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Constituent Assembly also performed legislative functions (acting as the Dominion Legislature / Provisional Parliament) starting from November 1947. Statement 2 is correct: whenever the Assembly met for legislative business, G.V. Mavalankar presided over it.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the major adoptions and approvals by the Constituent Assembly:
1. The National Flag of India was adopted on 22 July 1947.
2. The National Anthem and National Song were adopted on 24 January 1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Flag on 22 July 1947, and during its final session on 24 January 1950, it adopted the National Anthem ('Jana Gana Mana') and the National Song ('Vande Mataram').

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the sovereignty of the Constituent Assembly:
1. The Constituent Assembly was created by the British Parliament under the Cabinet Mission Plan and was fully sovereign from its very first meeting on 9 December 1946.
2. The Indian Independence Act of 1947 declared the Assembly a sovereign body that could abrogate or alter any law made by the British Parliament in relation to India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Assembly was NOT sovereign at its inception in December 1946, as it was bound by the limitations of the Cabinet Mission Plan. Statement 2 is correct: the Indian Independence Act, 1947 made the Assembly fully sovereign.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'Objectives Resolution':
1. It was moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in the Constituent Assembly in December 1946 and unanimously adopted in January 1947.
2. It explicitly declared India as a 'Sovereign Democratic Republic' and guaranteed social, economic, and political justice to all citizens.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Nehru moved the resolution on 13 December 1946, and the Assembly adopted it unanimously on 22 January 1947. Its core tenets directly mirrored the ideals enshrined in the Preamble.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the operational timeline of the Constituent Assembly:
1. The Assembly completed its constitution-making task in exactly two years, eleven months, and eighteen days.
2. It held its last session on 24 January 1950, after which it ceased to exist entirely and left governance in a vacuum until the first general elections.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (2 years, 11 months, 18 days). Statement 2 is incorrect because the Constituent Assembly did not cease to exist on 24 January 1950; instead, it converted itself into the Provisional Parliament of India until the formation of a new parliament in 1952.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the other key functions and roles of the Constituent Assembly:
1. It elected Dr. Rajendra Prasad as the first President of India on 24 January 1950.
2. It ratified India's membership of the Commonwealth in May 1949.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Assembly elected Dr. Rajendra Prasad as India's first President on 24 January 1950, and earlier ratified India's membership to the Commonwealth of Nations in May 1949.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding committees of the Constituent Assembly:
1. The Drafting Committee, headed by B.R. Ambedkar, was tasked with preparing the draft of the new Constitution.
2. The Union Powers Committee was headed by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (Drafting Committee was headed by B.R. Ambedkar). Statement 2 is incorrect because the Union Powers Committee and Union Constitution Committee were headed by Jawaharlal Nehru, whereas Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel headed the Provincial Constitution Committee and Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights and Minorities.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the legal transition on 26 January 1950:
1. The Government of India Act of 1935 and the Indian Independence Act of 1947 were formally repealed by Article 395 of the Constitution.
2. The Privy Council Jurisdiction (Abolition) Act, 1949, ended appeals to the Privy Council in London and transferred final appellate jurisdiction to the Supreme Court of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Article 395 repealed the GOI Act 1935 and Indian Independence Act 1947. Furthermore, ordinary legislation passed by the Constituent Assembly, such as the Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act 1949, solidified India's judicial sovereignty.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the criticism and composition of the Constituent Assembly:
2. It was criticized by some critics for not being a fully representative body because its members were indirectly elected by the provincial assemblies rather than through universal adult franchise.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct? (Note: Consider single statement-based format for rigorous testing)
1. All members of the Constituent Assembly were nominated directly by the British Viceroy without any elections.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because members were not nominated by the Viceroy; rather, they were elected indirectly by the provincial legislative assemblies. Statement 2 is correct: critics frequently pointed out the lack of direct election via universal adult franchise during its formation.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of B.R. Ambedkar in the Constituent Assembly:
1. B.R. Ambedkar was initially elected to the Constituent Assembly from Bengal and later, after partition, re-elected from the Bombay Presidency.
2. As the Chairman of the Drafting Committee, he steered the final draft of the Constitution through exhaustive debates and earned the title of 'Father of the Indian Constitution'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Ambedkar was first elected from East Bengal (which went to Pakistan post-partition), and subsequently re-elected from Bombay through the efforts of M.R. Jayakar. His stellar leadership of the Drafting Committee earned him the title of 'Father of the Indian Constitution'.
